builder_source_grounding.reason: Conservation is explicitly checked after each completed tick. Terminal arrivals are removed from queues before entering counters; dispatch moves snapshot stock to future queues. The suggested counterexample counts departure as delivery, contrary to the stated clock.
Canonical-root hash fixes one split before attribute draws. Quota failure is a stop, not reassignment or replacement. A uniform distribution over topological isomorphism classes is not claimed.
Tuple alternatives are explicitly in cyclic lexicographic order, so the last wraps to the first. Nontrivial eligibility and shortfall disposition are already required.

Opposite-label orientation balance is explicit per family and split, with P4 the base for CF-2. Same-label strata are also balanced. No per-root balance is asserted; inability to fill quotas is a feasibility stop.

Both views explicitly contain layer roles, source/sink, horizon and turnaround coefficient. The learned return bridge is the declared architectural bias under the narrowed hypothesis, not extra observation. Raw-view parity still requires later implementation verification.

Resampling roots with replacement is the stated clustered bootstrap. Common root draws preserve shared-data covariance across model contrasts. Models are not retrained in bootstrap replicates; family initialization draws are independent. Statistical calibration remains a separate uncompleted gate.

review_evidence.limitation: The builder rejects or narrows the six Qwen objections by the cited specification; this is not a reviewer ACCEPT. The second review produced no usable verdict. No claim of completed review or empirical validation is made.
remaining_gates: separately authorized generator feasibility and evaluator calibration

builder_source_grounding.reason: Section 2 specifies D_A >= 3/5 at inclusive H_A=10 and D_B >=3/10 at H_B=18. Section 3 expressly assigns threshold equality to class one and defines absorbing counters. Positive and negative strata refer to these task targets. Removing the quantity thresholds in favor of mere reachability would change the benchmark rather than repair it.

builder_source_grounding.reviewer_claim: kappa is undefined because transport tokens carry no carrier
builder_source_grounding.reason: One queried carrier is drawn per instance (section 5), with values K0/K1 (section 2); CF-1 changes that query while holding the whole world fixed. All dispatches in that instance use the selected channel. The specified scalar-stock system does not posit mixed-carrier tokens requiring separate token labels. Independent reference code must bind that same query explicitly.

The query is the per-instance carrier selected for the outcome and supplied to both raw views. CF-1 is operationally query K0 versus K1 in the same graph. No new carrier ontology or per-node default is needed.

builder_source_grounding.reviewer_claim: node embeddings cannot use carrier because nodes do not own carrier
builder_source_grounding.reason: The model conditions each node state on the shared input query; it does not assert that nodes possess a physical carrier attribute. The same query is available to F_G. Adding a per-node carrier or deleting conditioning would change the declared comparison without a demonstrated error.

builder_source_grounding.reviewer_claim: CF-7 preserving two effective channels requires p(K0)=p(K1)
builder_source_grounding.reason: CF-7 compares each channel before versus after tuple replacement, not K0 versus K1 within a tuple. At delay 2, tuples (p0=1/2,p1=1,c=1/2,r=0) and (p0=1/2,p1=1,c=1,r=1/2) both yield (a0=1/4,a1=1/2). Permeabilities differ and the distinct tuples preserve both channels. This analytic equality refutes the impossibility claim; it does not prove full dataset eligibility or quota feasibility.
